title: Tone.js — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Tone.js's rich face: the second Gotcha's claim put under plain Web Audio — sixty frequency pushes a second against the same equation run per sample, measured in what is rendered and handed to the ear blind — and the Recipe's shipped explorer gathered beside its own lines. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.
grain: The page's own ## grain. Only Gotchas and Recipes carry pieces; Gotchas is one section holding both dated gotchas and the community list, so its one stamp covers all of it.

offers.what: The second Gotcha's reason ("because the parameter automation is rendered at audio rate by Web Audio's internal scheduling") is right but incomplete. setValueAtTime holds each value until the next push, and the held step is applied on the exact sample, so the 60 Hz staircase is rendered at audio rate: Chromium's offline render matches a bare phase accumulator (the challenger's recompute). What it leaves out is why sixty a second is enough: the oscillator turns the staircase into a phase with no jumps, and the beat it follows is a few hertz, slow next to the frame rate. Measured in Chromium's Web Audio (plain OscillatorNode, not Tone), Δf = 2 Hz: beat 1.733 · 0.873 · 0.282 Hz pushed against 1.732 · 0.872 · 0.282 per sample (Adler 1.732 · 0.872 · 0.282) at K = 0.5 · 0.9 · 0.99; both lock at K = 1.00 = K_c on a 0.01 grid; the staircase's traces 60 Hz from the tones are at −72.5 dB re the tones (per sample −140.1). Suggest adding the missing half: "…and the beat it has to follow is far slower than the frame rate."

"Sample-coherent enough for audio-rate carriers in the 100–500 Hz range" names the wrong variable. The carrier enters neither edge; the frame rate against the coupling and the gap does. Narrowed to what the measurements show: (a) the lock shudders once K·cos φ* passes rate/2π, onset K = 9.6 · 4.9 · 3.4 Hz at 60 · 30 · 20 pushes a second (predicted 9.60 · 4.88 · 3.34). At the page's 60 frames that is past the explorer's 6 Hz K slider (11.3 Hz even at the widest gap that can still lock), so inside the page's ranges it is a condition only at 30 frames a second or fewer, including the explorer's own 1/20 s clamp (at K = 6 the locked gap swings 19.5 Hz at 30 and 24.2 at 20; 0.00 at 60). (b) With the tones more than half the frame rate apart the push aliases the beat: at 120 and 220 Hz with K = 6, both inside the explorer's sliders, the pushed tone carries a line 20 Hz off at −19.2 dB where the coupled one has −124.4, and it lacks the coupled pair's real line 100 Hz off (−47.4 against −30.4 dB). That is only where the tones are too far apart to lock (K_c = 50), so it limits "sample-coherent", not "enough to feel locking". Suggest: enough while the gap stays well under half the frame rate and K under about rate/2π (9.6 Hz at 60 frames a second, 4.9 at 30).

An added caveat, modelled offline and not timed on a device. The pushed tones aren't coupled to each other: the model is, and the tones follow it open loop. Every run still locks (the beat stops), but the locked phase gap is the model's plus whatever the model missed, and nothing pulls it back. Measured with K rising 0 → 1.5 over 6 s: on schedule the locked chord is shifted −0.4 dB from the coupled pair's (the explorer steps its phases before it pushes, so the tones run a frame behind its model: 2π·Δf/60 = 0.209 rad off φ*); with ±1 ms frame jitter and pushes on 128-sample render quanta, −0.4 to −0.5 dB; with one stalled frame of 60–500 ms during the drift (dt clamps at 0.05 s), −0.1 to −16.1 dB across eight runs. That range is a sample, not a bound: a shifted gap can also leave the chord up to +0.59 dB louder. A stall is real when a tab is backgrounded mid-play, which the page's own community list names. Suggest one line: "sample-coherent" holds the lock's frequency, not its phase, and a missed frame shifts the locked chord's level.

K_c = |Δf|/2 is right with K in hertz, as the explorer runs it: dθ/dt = 2π(f + K·sin Δθ). With the equation as the Gotcha writes it, dθ/dt = ω + K·sin(Δθ), K is in rad/s and the threshold is |Δω|/2 = π·|Δf|. Name K's unit (Hz), or write the equation with the 2π outside.

"Raising K past K_c first slows the beating, then collapses it": the slowing comes before K_c, on the way up, as √(Δf² − (2K)²) (measured 1.733 · 0.873 · 0.282 Hz at K = 0.5 · 0.9 · 0.99 with Δf = 2); past K_c it stops. Suggest: as K rises toward K_c the beating slows, and past it the beating stops.

The shipped explorer (Kuramoto Coupling/two-oscillators-coupling-explorer-audio.html, the Recipe's output) says in its own note that each frequency is f_j + (K/2π)·sin(θ_other − θ_j), but its code adds K·sin (K in Hz, as its slider is labelled), and the code is what the measurements match. Its readout "instantaneous beating rate" shows |f_A,inst − f_B,inst|, which below K_c swings between Δf − 2K and Δf + 2K rather than the beat heard, √(Δf² − 4K²). The note wants the /2π dropped; the readout wants a name like "frequency gap now". The fix is in the explorer file, not in this page's text.

verdicts.why: Caption only. Every number reproduces by a second route (numpy phase accumulators, my own meters), the blind A/B is sound, and the walk climbs. But the caption calls the page's reason wrong when it is only incomplete: a held step applied per sample is rendering at audio rate. It also lists the shudder (9.6 Hz at 60 pushes, past the 6 Hz slider) as a failure without its frame rate. Rewrite it to say the reason is incomplete, the shudder applies at 30 pushes/s or fewer, the alias sits where nothing can lock, and the stall is modelled, not timed.

pieces.title: sixty pushes a second, against the equation per sample
pieces.near: is enough to feel Kuramoto locking on two audio-rate sines
pieces.caption: **The second Gotcha, tested under Tone.** Five steps: two sines beating; coupled the page's way (sixty setValueAtTime pushes a second); the same pair run per sample in a worklet, with the pushed staircase drawn; then the test, rendered offline and measured. In the Gotcha's own situation the claim holds: the same beat rates to a thousandth of a hertz, the same lock K, and a staircase 73 dB down. The page's reason is right but incomplete. A held step applied on the exact sample is rendering at audio rate; what it leaves out is why sixty a second is enough: the beat is slow next to the frame rate. Where it stops, measured: at the page's 60 frames a second the lock starts to shudder at K = 9.6 Hz (11.3 at the widest gap that can still lock), past the explorer's 6 Hz K slider. It shows up only at 30 frames a second or fewer. Tones 100 Hz apart alias, but that is where nothing can lock (K_c = 50). A stalled frame, modelled offline and not timed, shifts the locked chord's loudness for good. The last step is a blind listen with a control round, because "enough to feel" is a claim about a listener. Chromium's numbers, not Tone's.

pieces.title: two-oscillator audio coupling explorer · Tone.js
pieces.caption: **The Recipe's own output.** The Study-tier explorer the Recipe describes, as it shipped into Kuramoto Coupling's bundle: two Tone.Oscillator sines, a K slider, a scope and the drift / pulling in / lock readout. It loads Tone 15.0.4 from the shelf's CDN, so it plays where the CDN is reachable. Its note's (K/2π) and its "instantaneous beating rate" readout are carried as an offer; the Gotchas piece above rebuilds the same pair without Tone.
